label: h right after g or 0, in a sequence starting with m/o/d/x (original phase)
explanation: Very sparse (28 dev steps). Fires almost only in the original phase: 82% of mass is on input h, with the previous token g (56%) or 0 (34%), and the sequence starting with m, o, d or x (100% of mass). Half the mass is at t=3, where the second token is usually n/u/g/0 (e.g. o n g [h], m o n f j u r g [h] is the max). Those three conditions are necessary for about 79% of the mass but are far from sufficient (precision about 2%). Adding t==3 and orig(1) in {n,u,g,0} raises precision to 58%, but recall drops to 50%. That points to a narrow hidden-state conjunction that the variables do not fully capture. A few outliers are on p, c, y, r and <DEL> after g/x/0 in m-initial sequences. Never fires in the copy phase, at t<3, or on repeated tokens. Magnitude is nearly flat (0.10-0.18); the largest values are h after g in m/o/x-initial sequences.
